## Behaviour
A small module (no third-party dependency, not coupled to the ledger or any forge) returns sparse, stable findings for one string: `zero_width` (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF), `bidi_control` (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069), `unicode_tags` (U+E0000-E007F), `confusable` (ASCII-lookalike ranges: fullwidth letters and digits, mathematical alphanumerics, Roman numeral forms, ligatures; Greek and Cyrillic only when the same string also holds ASCII letters or digits). Legitimate emoji are exempt: joiner sequences with at least two emoji bases, variation selectors and skin tone modifiers on emoji bases, keycaps on [0-9#*], and tag sequences only when they spell a recommended subdivision flag (England, Scotland, Wales). Vocabulary is pinned to a reviewed Unicode release with its source snapshot hashes in the module, never read from the host's Unicode database, so findings are identical on every machine. Findings are advisory: text is never normalized, hidden or rejected.

## Scenarios
- golden: a string holding a zero-width space, one with a right-to-left override, one with a tag-character payload and one with a Cyrillic letter among ASCII each report exactly their own finding. Prevents missed hidden-text classes.
- golden: family emoji with joiners, flag of Scotland, keycap 1 and a skin-toned hand report nothing. Prevents false positives on ordinary emoji.
- adversary: a black-flag tag sequence spelling an arbitrary word, or a joiner sequence mixing an emoji with an ASCII letter, is reported. Prevents the emoji exemption becoming a smuggling channel.
- adversary: pure Cyrillic text without ASCII is not flagged but the same word mixed with one ASCII letter is. Prevents false positives for legitimate non-Latin titles.
- seam: findings are identical when run under a different host Unicode database version (vocabulary is pinned in the module). Prevents drift across machines.

## Reference coverage
Reference text-scan module (no dedicated unit file); exercised by the read-suite triage walks (pinned findings without flagging emoji; tag sequences that do not spell a subdivision flag) and model-output graph-check walk (bidi): 3 tests map here, tested through commands as qew's rules require.

## Qew today
Missing. No scanning anywhere in qew.
seen.title: Build the stdlib text-scan engine: zero-width, bidi, Unicode tags, confusables, emoji exemptions
